# B00-RUNTIME-010 disposition: graphics-probe overlap exhausts GPU resources

## Preserved mandatory failure

Revision 03 startup-Release-RayTracing remains FAIL, exit 3221226505 / 0xc0000409 after 5.704 seconds, before close and without forced termination. Its raw SHA-256 remains 5749750fe228b318cc77d135962ad6d8aaaf35d3943c08f9a02b916f02fe2470; gzip SHA-256 remains a547ddd8679ce31a2a347080505cf0608869bf01b678da7e51e9033ad5dd7efe. No earlier capture, review, seal or registry was rewritten. This Revision 04 disposition is appended evidence, not a relabeling of that mandatory result.

## Ordered investigation and cause evidence

1. Six isolated launches used the unchanged Release executable (cb25301455b4fdeb46e4f1015c9913a5a59f2812dd965b25e7d8ea8ee13efc9c), source CWD, protected imgui.ini, accepted staged TBB, restricted PATH and unchanged 60-second/30-second normal-close probe. All six pass.
2. Separate Release application overlap launches use the original recorded relative starts: RayTracing first, Breakout about +219 ms, RigidBodySimulation about +363 ms. Round 1 passes; round 2 reproduces RayTracing 0xc0000409 at 3.375 seconds. Other apps pass. This reproduces the signature without the historical Editor build or Physics workload. Recorded actual starts retain scheduler variation.
3. Isolated sampled GPU memory is about 3944 MiB on the 8192 MiB RTX 3070 Laptop GPU. Concurrent ordinary round 1 reaches 7961 MiB. The short ordinary failure falls between samples: there is no claim to have measured its exact allocation peak. The GPU sampler is external, every two seconds; it begins during isolated round 2. No driver setting changes occur.
4. Six CDB -hd overlap probes pass. This demonstrates debugger timing sensitivity; it does not waive the ordinary failure.
5. A native DEBUG_ONLY_THIS_PROCESS event loop, with normal heap and no application breakpoints or upfront symbols, catches two further failures in four rounds. Attempt 01 captures a second-chance 0xc0000409, flags 1, parameter 7, registers and module hashes at 2.437 seconds. Its dump attempt fails because the diagnostic structure was not packed as minidumpapiset.h requires. The empty dump and old helper are preserved. After correcting only that helper, attempt 04 catches the same exception at 4.672 seconds and writes a valid full-memory dump, 4,137,440,798 bytes, SHA-256 35daea8c9191466406bc52834d95f3ee7ab806f031628f8bc8f94efac62be50a.
6. Offline CDB reads the actual exception, registers, all 48 thread stacks, module versions and driver code. Faulting PID 45276, TID 9280 (0x2440); RIP 00007ffc00baee7c, nvoglv64.dll + 0xFBEE7C, instruction int 29h. RCX and exception parameter are 7, FAST_FAIL_FATAL_APP_EXIT. The complete faulting stack is an NVIDIA worker path through nvoglv64 module offsets to kernel32/ntdll thread start. No RayTracing or TBB frame requests the fatal exit. Driver private symbols are unavailable: nearest exported names with large offsets do not identify true private functions or imply Vulkan usage.
7. Disassembly of the fatal caller identifies its stack message buffer. Reading that buffer from the failing dump yields the driver's GPU-memory exhaustion report, error 6, explicitly naming PID 45276 / TID 9280 / raytracing.exe. This directly ties the diagnostic to the captured fast-failing process. The matching historical Windows Application event 204268 at 2026-09-13T05:06:15.1352539Z, provider NVIDIA OpenGL Driver, names raytracing.exe PID 29040 / TID 25324 and the same error 6. The original helper did not log child PID; historical linkage uses executable and the 3.654-second timestamp match, not an invented historical PID cross-check.

## Classification against alternatives

| Candidate classification | Evidence-supported disposition |
| --- | --- |
| RayTracing application defect | Not demonstrated. Same candidate passes isolated; the captured fatal request is on an NVIDIA worker with the explicit resource message. No application memory-corruption or invalid viewport/texture-size fault was demonstrated. No RayTracing edit is justified. |
| Shared engine/runtime defect | Not demonstrated. Read-only source explains substantial baseline GPU allocation: BaseApp creates 8192-square cascade and point-shadow resources. Their sizes are unchanged. This allocation policy is outside this correction and is not redesigned. |
| TBB/runtime dependency defect | Not supported by fault state. Accepted tbb12.dll identity is unchanged; TBB worker stacks are waiting in the captured dump, and the fatal stack is in NVIDIA. No dependency change or provenance work is justified. |
| SDL/OpenGL/graphics driver failure | Established immediate failure mechanism: NVIDIA OpenGL worker explicitly terminates with FAST_FAIL_FATAL_APP_EXIT and error 6 resource diagnostic. Fault module nvoglv64.dll version 31.0.15.5244, SHA-256 6fc9e40cca16f29cef7b64001956b389c0ee620aa5585bbb1d963f4185ac1084. No evidence places the fatal exit in SDL. |
| Concurrency/resource-pressure sensitivity | Established for this validation setup: reproductions occur under application overlap; isolated probes pass; measured concurrent GPU occupancy approaches capacity; the failing process contains the matching resource exhaustion message. Exact failed GPU allocation and private driver budgeting are not available. |
| Probe/harness artifact | The process failure is real. The validation defect is concurrent scheduling of GPU-heavy acceptance probes on this machine, including the historic startup/teardown overlap. Correct the scheduling contract by serializing graphics acceptance through normal exit; never mark the failed raw process as PASS. |
| Unresolved intermittent failure | The original generic status now has an evidence-supported driver/resource/concurrency classification and a bounded harness correction. The precise internal driver allocation/budgeting decision remains opaque; absence of all possible application/driver defects is not claimed. This does not authorize simultaneous-app acceptance or a driver/application redesign. |

## Minimum correction and acceptance boundary

Only the new Revision 04 validation helper changes scheduling. Its acceptance command holds a Windows named mutex, refuses to start when an application probe or CDB is already present, and runs RayTracing, Breakout, RigidBodySimulation and RayTracing serially, waiting for normal exit and protected-layout restoration after each. Deliberate overlap remains an explicitly named diagnostic mode. No production or prior helper is edited. No build generation, compilation, runtime staging, dependency, driver or resource edit is required.

Final acceptance uses fresh serial Release probes plus the hash-verified complete Revision 03 acceptance matrix for all unchanged checks. The original failing mandatory record stays FAIL; the new RayTracing acceptance capture is a distinct measurement under the corrected scheduling contract. Final status depends on those fresh probes and the complete final integrity seal; later passes alone were never used to dismiss the failure.

## Limits and sources

The dump captures the earliest delivered fatal event before it is continued. Dump writing and hashing extend the capture's wall time while the process is stopped; 4.672 seconds is the fault time. The earlier uninstrumented reproduction cannot retrospectively supply a stack. All its available output and modules are retained. Release first-party symbols and NVIDIA private symbols are absent; raw addresses/stacks and loaded identities remain available. Optional !peb / !address queries lack OS type symbols and are recorded as unavailable, not passing. No symbol/toolchain changes were made.

The SDK winnt.h defines FAST_FAIL_FATAL_APP_EXIT as 7 and stack-cookie failure as 2. [Microsoft fast-fail documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cpp/intrinsics/fastfail?view=msvc-170) explains the exception parameter. [Microsoft CDB guidance](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/debugger/debugging-a-user-mode-process-using-cdb) documents normal-heap debugging. [NVIDIA's explanation](https://nvidia.custhelp.com/app/answers/detail/a_id/3553) describes the resource-exhaustion message and also notes command-stream limits as another possible cause; the concurrency attribution here rests on the local controlled comparison, measured pressure and actual dump, not that generic article alone.
